Solve the pair of equations $29x+31y=209$ and $31x+29y=211$.

text: In a quiz, Riya scored 12 marks more than Arjun. Twice Arjun's score is 6 more than Riya's score. Form a pair of linear equations and find the scores of both.

Two scooters start at the same time from towns 36 km apart. If they ride towards each other, they meet in 1.5 hours. If they ride in the same direction, the faster one catches the slower in 6 hours. Find the speed of each scooter.

The monthly incomes of Neha and Kabir are in the ratio $7:5$ and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio $3:2$. Each of them saves ₹4000 a month. Form a pair of linear equations and find their monthly incomes.
A bike rental shop charges a fixed booking fee plus a fixed rent for each day. Ravi paid ₹1950 for a 3-day rental and Sana paid ₹4150 for a 7-day rental. Find the booking fee and the daily rent.

Meena invested two sums of money, one at 6% and the other at 9% simple interest per year, and received ₹1500 as interest in a year. Had she invested the first sum at 9% and the second at 6%, she would have received ₹150 more in a year. Find the two sums.
A two-digit number is such that the product of its digits is 18. When 63 is subtracted from the number, its digits are interchanged. Find the number.

The floor of a rectangular hall keeps the same area if its length is reduced by 3 m and its breadth increased by 2 m. The area also stays the same if the length is increased by 3 m and the breadth reduced by 1 m. Find the length, breadth and area of the floor.
Six years ago, Meera was four times as old as her son. Four years from now, she will be twice as old as her son. Find their present ages.

In a test, Tanvi answered all the questions. If 4 marks were given for each right answer and 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer, she would score 66. If 3 marks were given for each right answer and 2 marks deducted for each wrong answer, she would score 42. How many questions were there in the test?

A science museum sells two kinds of entry tickets: a child ticket for ₹40 and an adult ticket for ₹90. On one Sunday it sold 300 tickets in all and collected ₹21000. Let $x$ be the number of child tickets and $y$ the number of adult tickets sold that day.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Write the pair of linear equations for this situation.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: How many adult tickets were sold that day?

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: If the price of a child ticket had been ₹10 less, with the same numbers of tickets sold, how much would the museum have collected?

text: For its annual day a school rents 80 pieces of furniture in all, chairs and tables. A chair is rented at ₹40 and a table at ₹150, and the total rent is ₹5400. Let $x$ be the number of chairs and $y$ the number of tables rented.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Write the pair of linear equations for this situation.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: If the school still rents 80 pieces in all but can spend at most ₹6500, what is the largest number of tables it can rent?

text: A car rental company offers two plans. Plan A charges a fixed ₹500 plus ₹12 per km driven. Plan B charges a fixed ₹800 plus ₹9 per km driven. Let $y$ be the total charge in rupees for a trip of $x$ km.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Write the pair of linear equations giving the charge under each plan.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: For what distance do the two plans cost the same, and what is that cost?

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: A family plans a trip of 160 km. Which plan should they choose, and how much will they save?
